result: The manuscript establishes the composition and known properties of the CoREST complex (LHC), which contains HDAC1, LSD1, and CoREST1 in 1:1:1 stoichiometry, and describes the established biological roles of these components in gene silencing.
evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C13, C88-C89 describe established knowledge about the CoREST complex composition and function, supported by citations to prior literature and confirmed by experimental data (Figure 2A). These are well-established facts serving as background for the study.

result: LHC exhibits bi-phasic demethylase kinetics with H3K4me2 peptide substrates, with distinct kinetic parameters for each phase, and this behavior persists despite varying buffer conditions. The complex remains intact during the reaction.
evaluation: Claims C14-C22 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2B-C and supplementary figures showing bi-phasic kinetics, kinetic parameters, and complex stability. Claim C78 is speculative about the mechanism but acknowledges uncertainty. The experimental observations are well-documented.

result: DNA (≥146 bp) dramatically activates LHC demethylase activity on H3K4me2 peptides (36-fold maximum, EC50 = 63 ± 15 ng/μL) and abolishes the lag phase, with shorter DNA fragments (60 bp) showing no effect.
evaluation: Claims C23-C29 are well-supported by dose-response data in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3. Claims C79-C80 are appropriately labeled as speculation about the mechanism. The experimental findings are robust and reproducible.

result: BHC80 modulates LHC demethylase activity by markedly inhibiting the second phase of the bi-phasic reaction at stoichiometric or higher concentrations, with saturation at 200 nM and minimal effect on the initial phase.
evaluation: Claims C30-C32 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 showing dose-dependent effects of BHC80 on LHC kinetics. The observations are clearly documented.

result: H3K14 acetylation strongly inhibits LHC demethylase activity toward H3K4me2 (~20-fold reduction in Km and kcat), and this is an intrinsic property of LSD1. The inhibition likely occurs through an intramolecular mechanism involving the negatively charged region near K14 in the LSD1 active site.
evaluation: Claims C2-C3, C33-C43 are supported by kinetic data in Figure 3 showing dramatic inhibition by K14ac in the presence of SAHA. Claims C42-C43 confirm this is an LSD1 property. Claims C65-C69 provide mechanistic interpretation based on structural data from cited literature. The experimental evidence is strong.

result: The use of depsipeptide (ester linkage) in the synthetic H3 N-tail significantly improved sortase-mediated ligation conversion from <40% to ~90%, offering advantages over other semisynthetic methods.
evaluation: Claims C44 and C82 are supported by experimental data in Figure 4A-B showing improved ligation efficiency. The comparison with other methods (C82) is appropriately contextualized with citations. This is a methodological advance.

result: LHC demethylates H3K4me2 nucleosomes only when DNA is extended to 185 bp (20 bp overhangs), with activity ~55-fold slower than peptide substrates. No demethylation was detected with 146 bp nucleosomes.
evaluation: Claims C45-C48 are supported by western blot data in Figure 5A-B showing DNA length-dependent demethylation and inhibition by corin. Claims C85-C86 cite prior literature consistent with these findings. The experimental evidence is clear, though the low rate limits detailed characterization.

result: LHC shows marked deacetylase selectivity for H3K9ac over H3K14ac (~7-fold) in nucleosomes, but this selectivity is lost with isolated H3 protein. Deacetylation is much faster than demethylation and likely precedes it.
evaluation: Claims C4-C5, C49-C54 are supported by western blot data in Figure 6 and kinetic data in Table 1 showing position-dependent deacetylation rates in nucleosomes but not in isolated H3. Claims C62-C63, C76-C77 provide appropriate interpretation. This is a key finding of the manuscript.

result: Hydroxamic acid-containing nucleosomes (H3K9Hd and H3K14Hd) inhibit LHC with similar Ki values (40-60 nM), indicating similar accessibility to the HDAC1 active site. This suggests the K9ac/K14ac selectivity is not due to simple steric differences but to subtle active site interactions.
evaluation: Claims C6, C55-C61 are supported by inhibition data in Figure 7 showing similar Ki values for K9Hd and K14Hd nucleosomes despite different deacetylation rates for K9ac and K14ac. The inference (C61) is logical and well-supported by the data.

result: H3K4me2/H3K14ac represents a privileged modification pair that is especially resistant to CoREST processing, suggesting the complex will be limited in silencing chromatin marked by H3K14ac. This selectivity may be a general property of class I HDAC complexes.
evaluation: Claims C70-C71, C83 are well-supported inferences from the experimental data showing dual resistance (demethylation and deacetylation). Claims C73-C75 provide supporting evidence from cited cellular studies and computational work. This is the main biological conclusion of the study.

result: The authors speculate that recruitment of LHC by DNA-binding transcription factors like REST would enhance targeting, and that hydroxamic acid nucleosomes may be useful for structural studies.
evaluation: Claims C64 and C81 are explicitly speculative and appropriately labeled as such. They represent reasonable hypotheses for future work but are not tested in this manuscript.

result: The purified LHC complex is stable for up to 2 weeks when stored at 4°C at ~5 μM concentration.
evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by experimental observations during the study and is consistent with the size exclusion data (C22) showing complex integrity.
